target: UTM-bundled QEMU, AArch64 PCI, one vCPU, disposable writable RedSea VirtIO fixture
command: QEMU=build/utm-qemu-probe/qemu-probe QEMU_VIRT='-L /Applications/UTM.app/Contents/Resources/qemu -machine virt,accel=hvf,gic-version=3 -cpu host -smp 1 -m 1024 -device virtio-ramfb -device virtio-keyboard-device -device virtio-tablet-device' ZEAL_COMPAT_LOG_PATH=build/tosmisc-malformed-repair-final-qemu.log python3 -u scripts/check-compat.py --pci --quick --probe-raw-redsea-geometry malformedrepair
result: pass: malformed bounded directory repair preserves the referenced allocation and leaves the volume valid
verified: The test uses a private disposable disk with a 128-sector writable RedSea fixture; no host disk or SD card is modified.
FilesFind returns BROKENDIR with its actual first sector (base+127), two-sector size, and directory attribute, despite its extent crossing the volume boundary.
Stock DiskCheck('D', TRUE, FALSE) reports one consistency error, does not clear allocation bitmap bit 126, and RedSeaValidate('D') still succeeds.
A subsequent read-only DiskCheck still reports the malformed extent, and the guest returns 42 with zstatus failed=0.
scope_note: This covers one malformed bounded directory and its referenced first allocation on a disposable RedSea fixture. It does not cover FAT32, arbitrary on-disk corruption, live UTM app interaction, or physical Raspberry Pi behavior.
